USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Finalize the Phase One agreement and hold off on the December 15 List 4B tariff hike (~$160B of consumer goods) to lock in the concessions China has already committed to on paper — roughly $40–50B in annual US agricultural purchases plus IP and currency terms. Do not escalate by letting the Dec 15 duties go into force; the deal is on the doorstep (reportedly the administration is already laying groundwork to delay it) and seizing it converts our hardline leverage into a signed win before the holiday season and the 2020 election. Pair this with continued deputy-level talks to get the text on paper.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is moderate, not existential. The tariff war has produced a material but contained drag — industrial production is roughly flat to slightly negative and the farm belt remains exposed to Chinese retaliation (neither side wants the $156–160B consumer-goods tranche to go live because it hits US shoppers on phones, laptops and toys for the first time). Yet the US economy is fundamentally sound: consumer sentiment has rebounded to 99.3, the Fed has already eased the fed funds rate from 2.40% to 1.55%, credit spreads are tightening, and the broad dollar is steady — so there is no recession spiral. The US holds the initiative: China agreed in principle (Oct 11) to large farm purchases and IP/currency concessions, and the Oct tariff hike on $250B was canceled. On the action side, letting the Dec 15 consumer-goods tariff take effect would raise costs on US consumers during the holidays, likely trigger renewed Chinese retaliation against US agriculture, and endanger the in-principle deal — a self-inflicted political and economic wound amid impeachment. A moderate de-escalation — delaying Dec 15 in exchange for a signed Phase One — is the right instrument: it salvages our leverage as a permanent, written concession rather than burning it on a counterproductive hike. This timing makes moderate rollback (partial_rollback) appropriate; full rollback would be premature since the text is not yet signed.
key_factors: Phase One agreed in principle Oct 11: ~$40-50B US ag purchases + IP/currency terms
Dec 15 List 4B tariff (~$160B consumer goods: phones, laptops, toys) is imminent
Reports as of Dec 10-11 that administration is preparing to delay Dec 15 tariffs
US macro solid: consumer sentiment 99.3, Fed funds cut to 1.55%, credit tightening
Trade-war drag present: flat/slightly negative IP, farm-belt and export exposure
Oct tariff hike on $250B already canceled; US holds negotiating leverage

USTR splits List 4; List 4B (cell phones, laptops, toys, apparel) delayed to Dec 15
Trump administration reportedly plans to delay 15% tariffs on ~$160B of Chinese goods set for Dec 15, laying groundwork for a Phase One deal
Neither side wants the 15% tariff on $156B of Chinese imports to go ahead since they hit consumer electronics, smartphones for the first time
Fed funds down 2.40% to 1.55%; consumer sentiment 99.3; IP roughly flat
